intent: Make usage_report.py import _fmt_h from the module that actually owns it, instead of reaching it through _usage_report_render, and stop tracking a generated TypeScript build cache.
scope: usage_report.py:43 - one import line split in two
bucket_catch/packages/frontend/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo - removed from tracking (file left on disk)
Non-goal: any behaviour change; no other module touched
changes: Split 'from _usage_report_render import _fmt_h, _render_report' into an import of _fmt_h from _usage_report_format and _render_report from _usage_report_render. After the previous commit's split, _fmt_h lives in the format module and the render module merely re-imports it for its own use in _methodology_section - so the old line made _usage_report_render a re-export barrel, which the brief explicitly rules out. The previous commit's message claimed no barrel existed; that claim was wrong and this commit makes it true.

git rm --cached on bucket_catch/packages/frontend/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo and added *.tsbuildinfo to .gitignore. It is a generated incremental-build cache that was tracked in a repo which otherwise blocks binaries, and it had been showing as dirty in every commit this session, forcing pre-commit to stash on each one.

verification.evidence: 143 passed, unchanged from before the import change.

Generated a full report from today's real atop logs (28 samples). This is the check that matters for an import change: a wrong module path is a runtime ImportError that unit tests importing the modules directly would not necessarily surface.
Reports '.gitignore:412:*.tsbuildinfo', so the new rule matches the file that was previously tracked.

risks: None for the import: _fmt_h is the same function object either way, and the module that defines it has no side effects at import time beyond two integer constants.
Untracking tsbuildinfo means a fresh clone builds without a warm incremental cache. That is the intended behaviour for a build artifact and costs one slower first `tsc -b`.
rollback: git revert the commit. usage_report.py returns to the single combined import (still functional, just routed through the barrel), and tsconfig.tsbuildinfo becomes tracked again.
After rollback, confirm pytest linux_configuration/tests still reports 143 passed and that usage_report.py still runs.
